title: Prefix Sums
summary: Sum any range in O(1) after one pass

steps.title: Lots of range questions
steps.body: What's the sum of a[l..r]? Asked once, just add it up. Asked q times, that's O(n) each and O(n · q) in total: 10¹⁰ when n and q are 10⁵.

steps.title: Running totals
steps.body: p[i] is the sum of the first i numbers. Then the sum of a[l..r] is p[r + 1] - p[l]. Build p once in O(n), then answer every range in O(1).

steps.title: Watch p fill up for a = [2, 4, 1, 5]

frames.note: Done. p[4] = 12 is the sum of everything

steps.why: p starts at 0 and adds one number at a time: 0, 3, 4, 6.

steps.prompt: p = [0, 2, 6, 7, 12]. What is the sum of a[1..2]?
p = [0, 2, 6, 7, 12]. What is the sum of a[0..3]?

steps.why: p[r + 1] holds a[0..r]. Subtracting p[l] removes a[0..l-1].

steps.prompt: Why does p have n + 1 slots, with p[0] = 0?
options: Ranges starting at 0 need no special case
steps.why: sum(0, r) is just p[r + 1] - p[0], so no if is needed.

options: Sums of many ints can pass 2 · 10⁹
steps.why: 10⁵ numbers up to 10⁹ add up to 10¹⁴, far past int.
Make room for n + 1 totals, then add one number at a time.

steps.prompt: n numbers and q range queries. Total time?
steps.why: O(n) to build p, then O(1) for each query.

steps.prompt: Match each value to its meaning
steps.why: Every range is the difference of two running totals.

steps.title: Prefix sums + a map
steps.body: a[l..r] sums to k when p[r + 1] - p[l] = k, so you need an earlier prefix equal to p - k. Walk once, count every prefix seen so far, and look up p - k.

frames.note: p = 1. Look for 1 - 2 = -1: never seen. Record 1
p = 2. Look for 0: seen once, so ans = 1. Record 2
p = 3. Look for 1: seen once, so ans = 2
ans = 2: [1, 1] at the start and at the end

options: It counts subarrays that start at index 0
steps.why: The empty prefix has sum 0. Without it, a[0..r] = k is never counted.

steps.prompt: a = [3, 4, 7], k = 7. How many subarrays sum to 7?
Which earlier prefix are you looking for?
steps.why: p - (earlier prefix) = k, so the earlier prefix is p - k.

steps.prompt: Put the loop body in order
steps.why: Look up before you record p, or with k = 0 you'd count an empty subarray.

steps.title: Why not a sliding window?
steps.body: A window works when growing it always grows the sum. Negative numbers break that: adding one can make the sum smaller. The map doesn't care about signs.

steps.why: Three pairs [1, -1], [-1, 1], [1, -1] and the whole array.

steps.prompt: n = 10⁵ with a map. Total time?
steps.why: n steps, each a map lookup of O(log n). unordered_map gets close to O(n).

steps.prompt: Which problem is this pattern for?
options: Count subarrays with sum exactly k
Find x in a sorted array
steps.why: Prefix sums turn any subarray sum into the difference of two prefixes.
